subject: one-child policy
title: What If a Country Allowed Only One Child? China Did for 35 Years

scenes.text: What if a country allowed every family one child? China did. The bill came due decades later.
In 1980, the rule went nationwide. In 1979, women averaged 2.8 children. By the mid-1990s, 1.5.
Families wanted that one child to be a boy. At birth, the normal ratio is about 105 boys per 100 girls. China's climbed to 117.
By 2016, the country had about 34 million more men than women. Millions who will never find a wife.
Then the shape of the family flipped. One adult, two parents, four grandparents to support. Demographers call it the 4-2-1 problem.
The limit ended in 2016. Births kept falling anyway, to about one child per woman by 2024. The policy switched off. The habit didn't.

description:
What if a country allowed only one child per family? China enforced that limit from 1980 until 2016, and its effects are still unfolding.
The fertility rate fell from 2.8 in 1979 to 1.5 by the mid-1990s. A preference for sons pushed the sex ratio at birth to about 117 boys per 100 girls at its peak, and by 2016 China had around 34 million more men than women. One child now faces supporting two parents and four grandparents. The limit was lifted in 2016 and all limits removed in 2021, but the fertility rate kept falling to about 1.0 by 2024.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: China's government has claimed the policy prevented 400 million births; many demographers put the figure at about half that. What rule would you change if you ran a country? And what should we run through next?
